$comment: The defect the story names outright: an intent nothing on the menu serves, answered with a confident dispatch.
The CI workflow scaffolds a pipeline and no menu item runs a suite or repairs a failing test, so the user is
sent somewhere that cannot answer and is told nothing about it.
Its threshold is zero rather than a rate.
A frozen copy of one case of the live corpus, of the menu it is scored against, and of the user's message.
Those three plus the reply are the whole input to scoreCase, so all three are stored here rather than read
live: a replay has to keep scoring the scenario it was derived against after the corpus moves on, and
npm run test:eval-routing-data already holds the live corpus against the shipped menu.

expected.rationale: No menu item executes a suite or repairs failing tests. CI scaffolds a pipeline and review judges tests; neither runs nor fixes anything, and dispatching either sends the user somewhere that cannot answer.

inputs.intent: Our CI is red. Run the suite, find the failing tests, and fix them for me.

derivation: The oracle expects decline and the action is route, so actionCorrect is false and confidentRouteOnUnservable is
decidingTokens is [run, fix]. The reason carries neither, so tokensFound is 0.
declineOk is false because the action is not a decline. unroutedClearIntent is false: that control counts the
opposite mistake, and it is only ever counted on a case with one right answer.

answer.reason: your pipeline is red, so the continuous integration workflow is the place to start
